newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Sandinistas say bandits threaten Nicaragua vote.
newsitem.headline: Sandinistas say bandits threaten Nicaragua vote.

text.p: An armed gang roaming the mountains of northern Nicaragua on Sunday prevented some peasants from voting in hotly contested presidential elections, one of the leading political parties charged.
An army spokesman in Managua, Capt. Milton Sandoval, said he had heard the reports but was unable to confirm them.

Jose Gonzalez, secretary of the leftist Sandinista Front in the northern city of Matagalpa, said the bandits -- believed to be loosely linked to former Contra rebels -- had threatened peasants in areas where army vigilance is lax.

"Armed groups are intimidating people in the rural sector between Matiguas and Rio Blanco, threatening peasants so that they do not vote," he told Reuters, saying the reports had come through to his party's headquarters by radio.
He said there were no reports of bloodshed.

Matiguas and Rio Blanco are two towns in Matagalpa province about 100 miles (160 km) northeast of Managua. The area was a key battleground in the war by U.S.-backed Contras in the 1980s against the then-Sandinista government.
The army says some 400 disenchanted former Sandinista soldiers and ex-Contras continue to roam in bands in remote areas of Nicaragua. Some have threatened to disrupt the polls.

The Sandinistas recently said bandits in the Matiguas area supported the front-runner in the election, right-wing populist Arnoldo Aleman, who was just ahead of the left-wing Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega before the vote.
Gonzalez suggested that the bandits were impeding the voting to prevent peasants supporting Ortega.
